slot_note: re-root of the retired ET01 slot in oviya1301's wave 1; no seed note: the world is drawn for its calendarization step
niche: calendarizing three gas utilities' cycle-read and bimonthly-read residential sales into the calendar-month county series a heating assistance administrator files under the state's energy data standard, which sets the 2026-27 grant split
stakeholder_role: head of research at a statewide nonprofit that administers the state's heating assistance grant and compiles the gas utilities' data behind it

spine.entity: one AMI gas meter's validated daily consumption on one gas day

world.geography: United States, Michigan (fictional nonprofit, three gas utilities and a twelve-county northern region, all invented)
world.org_type: statewide nonprofit administering the state's heating assistance grant for the community action agencies, producing the calendar-month county gas series under the state's energy data standard

driver: A total each unit records over its own reading interval, one period or two long, is split onto fixed calendar periods by how fast it ran inside the interval, which a sample of units measured every day shows rising several-fold over a run of extreme days late in one period, so splitting by elapsed days moves that run's use out of the period it fell in for every interval that straddles it, most for the units read every second period, while scaling the daily-measured sample up instead carries its members' smaller size.
driver_concrete: Each county's calendar-January 2026 residential gas use is every Kestrel Valley, Northbank and non-AMI Pine Harbor bill's therms split across the days it covers by the daily use Pine Harbor's AMI accounts show (three to four times higher in the 19 to 31 January cold snap than in the mild weeks around it), not by days of service, so day-proration moves cold-snap therms out of January for every straddling interval, most in the counties Northbank reads every second month, and scaling the AMI accounts' January use up instead carries their newer, smaller homes.
stump: A competent solver nets the cancel and rebill lines, maps premises to counties, takes Pine Harbor's AMI accounts from their calendar-month bills, prorates every other bill's therms across the months it covers by days of service and splits the grant on those January totals, because use inside a bill follows the weather and the intervals straddling the late-January cold snap are split as if every day burned the same gas (the county figures are filled from the generator).
analyst_test: A strong analyst who cleans the three billing extracts and the AMI reads and reads every field right prorates each bill to calendar months by days of service, the standard way to calendarize billing-period data, which moves the late-January cold snap's therms out of January wherever an interval straddles it and under-allocates the counties read every second month, although the AMI accounts' daily reads show use is far from flat inside a bill.
domain_test: Calendar-month statistics built from billing-period returns are what an official statistics producer calendarizes against an indicator of activity inside each period (here the AMI accounts' daily reads), as statistical offices calendarize fiscal-period returns with a monthly indicator; the stump lives in heating use swinging with the weather inside each read interval, so moving the nouns to a series whose activity is flat within periods leaves day-proration right and the task empty.
layer1: three utilities' billing extracts in their own layouts: a 21-cycle monthly-read CIS export, a bimonthly-read export carrying prior and current read dates, and a utility that bills its AMI accounts on calendar months while its other accounts still read on cycles
cancel and rebill transactions: a corrected bill carried as a reversing line and a replacement line under the original bill number
an MDMS daily-read export keyed by meter with VEE quality codes (validated, estimated, edited), daylight-saving gas days and register rollovers
meter-to-account history with AMI installations during the winter, each leaving a short transition bill from the last cycle read to month end
premise county from a service-address file whose ZIP codes cross county lines
one utility billing CCF with a monthly heating-value factor beside billed therms
the state energy data standard (calendar-month residential therms by county) and each utility's field notes on its read-date convention

lineage.fate: built and solved in-house four times (rounds 1 to 4 on 2026-10-09 at 93.8, 80.2, 86.0 and 91.7, the main call landed in every round: the replay executed each rung as a routine step); three hardening loops spent; retired by the author on 2026-10-11
lineage.niche: a philanthropic trust's stabilisation offers to grantees whose income is falling, scored on twelve months of income built from the grantees' quarterly portal returns and their filed annual returns, run in-house for the first time after the bureau that computed six March rounds left
lineage.driver: A trailing four-period total at a cut-off runs only over periods whose year is closed by an annual filing on record at that cut-off, each period in the year its own record names, and only units holding a contract in force on the cut-off day are scored; a unit's contract can lapse between terms while the register still carries it from its first start to the renewed term's end, and because no unit was ever between terms at a published cut-off, scope read from the register's dates reproduces every published result, but at the first cut-off that finds a unit between terms that scope scores it on a true fall, offers it and re-splits the fixed pool with it in.
lineage.stump: A competent solver rebuilds the screen as held at the 30 September census, collapses the dual-grant returns, builds each grantee's twelve months from the identity on the register as held with every quarter in the year its own return runs within, gives back all 821 published rows, every offer and every rate, reads rule 4.1 against rule 2's census list and drops the 17 grantees whose year to 31 March 2026 has no annual return on the register, and strikes the offers at 34.79 cents on 10 names, because it takes scope from the grants register's start and end dates (start of the grant, end of its current term), which keep Ilam After School Care Society in, so it scores its true 13.62 per cent fall over the twelve months to June 2026 and offers it, when the Variations sheet shows that its term ended on 31 July 2026 and its renewal runs from 1 November 2026, nothing paid for August to October, so it held no operating grant in force at the census (rule 3.1), and the answer scores 132 grantees and strikes 42.55 cents on nine.

notes: Re-root of the retired task123 (ET01) slot on 2026-10-12, architecture 2. Subdomain seasonal-adjustment-official-time-series-production: the client's Survey Research & Official Statistics task type that serves ETL, here calendarizing billing-period returns into an official calendar-month series against an indicator of activity inside each period. stump_strategy time_semantics, the reviewer's key for billing-period to calendar-month conversion; the semantics-risk WARN is answered by the analyst test (every field and rule read right, day-proration still files the wrong split). Gap time leads (the evidence is a total over each account's own interval and the decision reads a calendar month); population second (the AMI accounts are a sample whose homes are newer and smaller than the region's). G4 attribution at transition: which month holds a straddling bill's therms; G2 the bill against the month as the unit; G14 the AMI accounts' January use carried onto the whole pool; G19 the state data standard as depth. Gate method_or_model_selection: the method that splits each interval. Shape 05: a fixed grant split across twelve counties. Calibration none: nothing scores the method; the AMI daily reads are the indicator the method needs, not a control. Personas drawn with guard.py names --geo 'United States' --seed 123.
